title: Pork and Apple Pie
subtitle: A raised shortcrust pie of seasoned pork and sharp cooking apple
excerpt: Seasoned pork shoulder and tart cooking apple in a sturdy shortcrust case, baked until the top is deep gold. The apple keeps the filling moist and cuts through the richness of the meat.
sourceNotes: British country cooking tradition; pork and apple is a longstanding regional pie combination across the West Country and the Midlands.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze once fully cooled. Reheat from frozen at 180C, covered with foil, for 30 minutes, then uncover for a further 10 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the pie the day before and refrigerate unbaked. Glaze and bake on the day, adding 5 minutes to the baking time.

content.text: Pork and apple is a pairing that works because the acid of the fruit lifts the fat of the meat. Use a Bramley or another sharp cooking apple, not an eating apple, or the filling turns sweet and cloying. The filling goes in raw, so the pie needs a full bake at a good temperature.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid

content.text: Combine the diced pork, apple, onion, sage, mustard powder, salt, pepper, and nutmeg in a large bowl. Mix well with your hands and leave to sit for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry on a lightly floured surface and line a 23cm deep pie dish. Leave a 2cm overhang around the edge. Chill while you prepare the lid.
Pack the filling firmly into the pastry case. It should mound slightly above the rim. Roll the remaining pastry into a lid.
Brush the overhang with beaten egg. Lay the lid on and press firmly around the edge to seal. Trim away the excess pastry and crimp the rim with a fork.
Brush the top all over with beaten egg. Cut two small slits in the centre to let out steam.
Bake for 20 minutes at 200C, then reduce to 180C and bake for a further 50 to 55 minutes until a skewer inserted through the slit feels hot when touched to your wrist.
Rest the pie for at least 15 minutes before slicing. This allows the juices to settle and the filling to firm up.

items.symptom: The pastry top is brown but the filling is still pink in the centre.
items.cause: The pie was not baked at full heat long enough, or the pork was cut too large.
items.fix: Cut pork into 1.5cm dice as directed. Cover the top with foil if it colours early and continue baking until the skewer test passes.

items.symptom: The filling leaks juice and makes the base soggy.
items.cause: The apple released a lot of liquid during baking.
items.fix: Add 1 tablespoon of plain flour to the filling mix to absorb the juice. Press the pastry base firmly against the dish before filling.

items.symptom: The lid shrinks and pulls away from the rim.
items.cause: The pastry was stretched rather than laid in.
items.fix: Always let the pastry settle into the dish under its own weight. Chill the assembled pie for 30 minutes before baking to relax the gluten.
